stories.title: US company’s AI lets Ukraine’s cheap kamikaze drones track targets on their own
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: US company is providing advanced AI capabilities to Ukraine's inexpensive kamikaze drones.
The deal involves equipping 50,000 Ukrainian drones with US-developed autonomous targeting AI.
The transaction is valued at $100 million, highlighting a significant military technology transfer.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by collapsing it to $O(1)$ per query.
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to efficiently manage persistent context and corpus retrieval.

stories.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
stories.author: Matthew Dressman
bullet_points: The rise of complex AI systems involves ensembles of specialized, coordinating agents, not just single models.
Existing AI abuse detection frameworks are inadequate because they primarily focus on single-turn or single-session threat models.
The research addresses a critical gap by proposing a method to detect harmful misuse across multiple, sequential AI sessions via capability accumulation.

stories.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection
stories.author: Jonathan Tapson
bullet_points: Introduces PRECOG, a novel retrieval mechanism designed for Edge Language Models.
Addresses the high prefill cost ($O(L_{context})$) associated with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) by collapsing it to $O(1)$ per query.
Leverages the inherent properties of State-Space Models (SSMs) to manage persistent context efficiently, overcoming limitations of traditional Transformer KV-caching.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.

Ollama currently serves a substantial community of 8.9 million developers.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when running through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference speeds.
The updated engine also demonstrates better memory efficiency when running large language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents run locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, offering significant speed improvements.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, ensuring all processing runs directly on the user's device.
The core value proposition is providing private, on-device AI assistance for coding tasks.

stories.title: China is Tesla's cash cow, but for how much longer?
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Tesla's Shanghai factory is experiencing record activity.
There are growing concerns regarding the long-term reliance of Tesla on the Chinese market.
The article suggests potential future risks or changes to Tesla's relationship with its Chinese operations.

stories.title: MedPRESS: A Multi-turn Benchmark for Patient-Pressure-Induced Medical Sycophancy in LLMs
stories.author: Niloy Farhan
bullet_points: Introduces MedPRESS, a new multi-turn benchmark specifically designed for evaluating LLMs in medical contexts.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM safety research by testing models under 'patient-pressure-induced sycophancy' rather than static questioning.
The benchmark consists of 600 medically grounded five-turn dialogues covering medication, self-care, and symptom triage.

stories.title: Mistral's Shieldstral: 3B open-weights model for multimodal moderation
stories.author: riadsila
bullet_points: Mistral has released Shieldstral, a new 3B open-weights model.
The model is specifically designed for multimodal content moderation tasks.
This contributes to the growing trend of open-source models being applied to safety and moderation challenges.

stories.title: IntelliJ IDEA Goes LSP: Java and Kotlin Intelligence Comes to VS Code, Cursor, and Agentic Flows
stories.author: blog.jetbrains.com via cgrinds
bullet_points: IntelliJ IDEA's advanced Java and Kotlin intelligence is being ported to other editors via LSP.
This integration brings powerful IDE features to VS Code, Cursor, and supports agentic workflows.
The move signifies a broader industry trend toward standardized, language-agnostic tooling via Language Server Protocol (LSP).

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically benefiting Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for more complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access and utilize current information.

stories.title: ‘Not healthy’ LLM use is more common than you think
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Popular science communicator Hank Green is stepping back from production due to criticism regarding his use of AI.
Green defended his AI usage, stating it was primarily for finding research sources, not for scriptwriting.
The incident highlights growing public and industry concerns about the 'healthy' and ethical integration of LLMs in content creation.

stories.title: Texas says data centers must pass an audit before connecting to the grid
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Texas is implementing a new audit requirement for data centers.
The audit must be completed before new data facilities can connect to the state energy grid.
The directive was issued by Governor Greg Abbott to PUCT and ERCOT, potentially slowing approvals.

stories.title: OpenAI says Apple's trade secrets lawsuit is "aggressive and oddly personal"
stories.author: Jamie John, Financial Times
bullet_points: OpenAI publicly criticized Apple's lawsuit regarding alleged trade secret infringement.
OpenAI asserted that it neither possesses nor desires any of Apple's trade secrets.
The dispute highlights ongoing legal tensions between major AI and tech industry players.

stories.title: An AI-supervised remote exam went so badly that 58,000 students must retake it
stories.author: Nate Anderson
bullet_points: An AI-supervised remote exam experienced significant failure.
The system's performance was flawed, leading to 58,000 students needing to retake the test.
The failure manifested in extreme score inflation, with top scores increasing fivefold.

stories.title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
stories.author: Li
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap between specialized AI applications in power systems and the need for reusable educational tools.
It proposes an Engineering-Grounded AI (EGAI) framework to bridge AI workflows with established power system engineering practices.
The framework aims to provide hands-on, executable material for interdisciplinary learners entering the energy sector.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a new unified embedding model designed for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in existing Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) by moving beyond encoder-style bidirectional architectures.
Aims to simplify multimodal embedding by integrating sparse and dense representations within a decoder-only framework.

stories.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs
stories.author: Ningxin Su
bullet_points: Introduces CoWAM, a new selective intervention layer designed to augment World Action Models (WAMs) in robotics.
CoWAM uses 'coordination contracts' to enforce constraints like synchronization, role compatibility, and collision convergence.
The system integrates typed admissibility checks and event-conditioned verification to justify policy changes based on predicted futures.

stories.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
stories.author: Jovan Stojkovic
bullet_points: The paper introduces AtumAI, a framework designed to automate the complex design of datacenter control-plane policies using Agentic AI.
Current off-the-shelf AI approaches are insufficient because they lack formal structure, making it difficult to enforce hard constraints.
The core problem addressed is the immense complexity and time required to manually design and prototype policies for modern, rapidly evolving hardware-software datacenter stacks.

stories.title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI
stories.author: Shahram Rahimi
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in current Generative and Agentic AI, which often lack sustained reasoning and self-regulation.
It proposes a taxonomy to categorize the fundamental cognitive capability gaps in modern AI systems.
The research points toward the need for Cognitive AI to evolve beyond simple language generation and task execution.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended generative AI outputs.
It highlights a gap where existing fairness definitions focus on input attributes, while generative audits examine output composition without clear targets.
The research suggests a need to move beyond simply supplying demographic targets to actively justifying them in AI generation.

stories.title: onepot-Bench 0: towards lab-aware in silico chemistry benchmarks
stories.author: Daniil A. Boiko
bullet_points: Language models are increasingly used in laboratory science for tasks like experiment planning and analysis.
Current evaluations struggle to accurately measure the complex, domain-specific intuition required for reliable lab decision-making.
The paper introduces 'onepot-Bench' to create benchmarks that are 'lab-aware' for evaluating these models.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: GradCuit introduces a novel method to improve LLM outputs by optimizing instance-specific latent states at test time.
It addresses a limitation in existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates was indirect, obscuring reasoning flow.
The technique allows for robust and interpretable latent reasoning by directly integrating optimizable states into the model's circuit.

stories.title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs
stories.author: Ningxin Su
bullet_points: Introduces CoWAM, a new selective intervention layer designed to augment World Action Models (WAMs) in robot policies.
CoWAM uses 'coordination contracts' to enforce constraints like synchronization, role compatibility, and collision convergence.
The system integrates typed admissibility checks and event-conditioned verification to justify policy changes.

stories.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality
stories.author: Yanze Guo
bullet_points: Diffusion models' reliance on stochastic inputs is constrained by deterministic pseudorandom number generation on finite hardware.
The structure of these pseudorandom orbits can be treated as a learnable input that influences model training and output quality.
A small MLP can be used to predict the next state of the orbit based on its historical values, linking randomness to optimization.

stories.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
stories.author: Chenyang Si
bullet_points: AURORA-LM proposes a new approach to language modeling by moving beyond discrete tokens to continuous latent spaces, aligning with trends in image/video generation.
The model addresses a key limitation in current continuous language models: maintaining high token-level fidelity while using autoencoded latents for diffusion.
It aims to preserve a high-capacity representation, avoiding the common practice of simplifying latents solely to accommodate the generative model.

stories.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
stories.author: Zilong Zheng
bullet_points: Introduces GradCuit, a method for optimizing latent states during LLM inference to improve output quality.
Addresses the limitation of existing methods where credit assignment for latent updates is indirect via decoded tokens.
Enables more robust and interpretable test-time latent reasoning by directly assigning credit to gradient flow.

stories.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
stories.author: Shu Wu
bullet_points: Introduces UEmbed, a new unified embedding model for multimodal tasks.
Addresses limitations in current Learned Sparse Retrieval (LSR) methods, which are often tied to bidirectional encoders.
Aims to improve multimodal retrieval by moving beyond reliance on auxiliary cross-modal modules.

stories.title: Who Should Be Generated? Justifying Demographic Targets in Open-Ended Generation
stories.author: Wenqing Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of justifying demographic targets in open-ended AI generation.
It highlights a gap in current fairness evaluation, which often assumes sensitive attributes are provided as input.
The research focuses on output-side demographic composition audits, noting that the comparison targets are usually supplied rather than theoretically justified.

stories.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
stories.author: Yang Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of current LLM context handling in long-running applications.
Introduces the concept of 'state continuity under context turnover' for persistent memory.
Proposes a method (LiveMem) to maintain a persistent state independent of the active context window.

stories.title: SWE-Touch: Benchmarking Coding Agents When Users Touch the Code
stories.author: Kang Liu
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Touch, a new framework to benchmark coding agents in real-world, shared development environments.
Addresses a gap in current benchmarks by testing how agents handle code changes made by human users during an ongoing task.
Utilizes 'Counter-Edits' to simulate plausible user modifications, stress-testing the agent's ability to understand and respond to collaborative code changes.

stories.title: Cultural Awareness is Represented but Not Decoded: Tracing Mythological Knowledge across 18 Open-Source LLMs
stories.author: Mika Hämäläinen
bullet_points: The study investigates how cultural knowledge, specifically mythological figures, is encoded across 18 open-source Large Language Models (LLMs).
Findings show LLMs exhibit a cultural bias, reliably recognizing major Western deities but struggling with less-represented traditions (e.g., Finnish, Slavic, Egyptian).
Researchers employed advanced interpretability techniques (linear probing, activation patching) to trace where this cultural default bias originates within the model architecture.

stories.title: Launch HN: EdotEnv (YC S26) – Quant Trading RL Envs to Teach LLMs Research
stories.author: Mzzzzz
bullet_points: EdotEnv is a new project focused on creating self-improving Reinforcement Learning (RL) environments.
The environments are derived from quantitative trading workflows, leveraging the market's inherent property of increasing difficulty with efficiency.
The goal is to provide more meaningful benchmarks for training and evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) beyond saturated traditional benchmarks.

stories.title: DeepSeek V4 Flash on a Single AMD MI300X
stories.author: zhoutong
bullet_points: DeepSeek V4 Flash model is being tested on a single AMD MI300X accelerator.
The headline suggests a focus on efficient deployment of a large language model (LLM) on specific hardware.
This indicates ongoing industry interest in optimizing LLM performance on AMD's high-end AI hardware.

stories.title: My Agent Orchestrator Burned 1-2M Opus Tokens Per Task. Here's the Postmortem.
stories.author: akashy
bullet_points: The article details a significant operational cost issue (1-2M Opus tokens) encountered while using an agent orchestrator.
The root cause was identified as a design flaw involving three cost multipliers applied to every request in a pure-delegation skill.
The solution involved implementing a PreToolUse hook to enforce budget constraints externally, rather than relying solely on prompt engineering.

stories.title: TokenMizer: Giving LLMs a Memory That Doesn't Forget Between Sessions
stories.author: shweta_mishra_b3c97874de9
bullet_points: Introduces 'TokenMizer,' a tool designed to give LLMs persistent memory across separate sessions.
It functions as a graph-memory proxy situated between the application and the OpenAI API.
Addresses a common limitation of LLMs by allowing them to retain context and information over time.

stories.title: Why AI Coding Agents Get Lost in Large Codebases
stories.author: siddharthakatiyar
bullet_points: AI coding agents are showing improved reasoning capabilities with modern LLMs.
The core challenge discussed is the difficulty these agents face when operating within large, complex codebases.
The article likely explores the limitations of current context window management and architectural design in AI tooling.
